**[p. 156]** Surah Maryam (peace be upon her)

Its central purpose is to show that He, glory be to Him, is characterized by all-encompassing mercy, by bestowing blessings upon all of His creation. This implies that He possesses all the attributes of perfection, which in turn implies comprehensive power to originate the extraordinary, which entails complete power, which necessitates the ability to resurrect and His transcendence above having offspring [because offspring exist only for one who is in need, and only one like the parent can be offspring]. Nor does He have any namesake, let alone any equal. This is indicated by the name of the surah, Maryam, because her story is the clearest evidence within it of complete power and all-encompassing knowledge. The most remarkable and most comprehensive of created beings is the human being. The most astonishing of the four modes of human generation, after being human itself, is that which came from a female without the intervention of a male. This is because it is the weakest mode, and the most remarkable element of it is that from such weakness there arises the strongest kind, namely a male, especially if he is granted the power of speech, knowledge and the Book in infancy, and he declares his complete safety, and so it is: no one, despite the multitude of enemies, could harm him in any way. In addition to this, she combined bringing forth fresh dates out of season from dry wood, and the flowing of water in an unusual place. And similarly, the surah is indicated by the letters that open it. The explanation is that the point of articulation of the **kaf** is at the far end of the tongue, adjacent to the throat and opposite the lower palate, and it is slightly further forward in the mouth than the **qaf**. Its attributes (**sifat**, the phonetic qualities of letters) include *hams* (voicelessness), *shidda* (plosiveness), *infitah* (openness), *istifal* (lowering) and *khafa'* (concealment). The point of articulation of the **ha'** is at the far end of the throat, but it is slightly closer to the tongue than the **hamza**. Its attributes include *hams*, *rakhawa* (softness), *infitah*, *istifal* and *khafa'*. The point of articulation of the **ya'** is the middle of the tongue and the upper palate. Its attributes include *jahr* (voicing), *rakhawa*, *infitah* and *istifal*, and this is its predominant quality. The point of articulation of the **'ayn** is the middle of the throat. Its attributes include *jahr* and an intermediate state between *shidda* and *rakhawa*, together with *infitah* and *istifal*. The point of articulation of the **sad** is the tip of the tongue and between the roots of the two lower incisors. Its attributes include *hams*, *rakhawa*, *itbaq* (emphasis), *isti'la'* (elevation) and *safir* (whistling).

Thus, the opening with these letters here is a sign, and God knows best, that the people of God in general, those mentioned in this surah and others, will at first, in the eyes of their opponents, be weak with great openness, as the **kaf** indicates. This was the state of the Prophet ﷺ when he first called people, for his matter became well known, but it was weak because of his people's denial, although they did not go to extremes in their denial. Then, in the early stages of the struggle, the matter comes to lowering, as the **ha'** indicates, and then it grows weaker and more concealed through the collusion of the arrogant against them. To this the recitation with *imala* (inclination of the vowel, a reading in which the vowel is pronounced toward the *ya'* sound) points. Nevertheless, there must be some kind of manifestation, as the openness of the **ha'** indicates, and to this the recitation with *fath* (the open vowel) points. This is as the Prophet ﷺ was when he openly reviled their gods, ridiculed their judgment and misled their fathers, and they stood against him as one band. So most of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, emigrated to Abyssinia, and Abu Talib feared the common masses of the Arabs, so he composed his famous *lamiyya* ode on that subject. The situation continued until the Quraysh forced them into the ravine (Shi'b Abi Talib). And in the middle of their affair, as the **ya'** indicates, and its recitation with *fath* indicates, they have strength together with softness, fame and lowering, and this is predominant over them in outward appearance, as the recitation with *imala* indicates. So their humiliation comes from behind glory, and their glory is clothed in humiliation. Whoever has experienced this knows it, and whoever has looked upon it with the eye of truth has witnessed it. This was also the case when those among the Quraysh rose up to annul the unjust document and bring them out of the ravine. Then came the deaths of Khadija, may God be pleased with her, and Abu Talib, and the Prophet ﷺ went out to Ta'if, but they turned him away, may my father, mother, self, child and eye be ransomed for him. When he drew near to blessed Makkah, he could not enter it without protection, so he hid in the cave of Hira' and sent for someone to grant him protection. Then he sent again until al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi granted him protection, and he and those who obeyed him took up arms and brought him in, peace be upon him, until he circled the House. Then God, glory be to Him, decreed that al-Mut'im would be killed as a disbeliever at Badr, after the Prophet ﷺ had striven for his safety and enjoined that he should not be killed, so that it might be known that He, glory be to Him, is free to choose in the generality and particularity of His mercy, lest the disobedient despair or the obedient feel secure. **[p. 159]** Then, when their affair rises from the middle and ascends, it grows strong, as the **'ayn** indicates, so it lies between strength and softness, with openness, fame, and some lowering in part of the matter. This was the Prophet's ﷺ state at the pledge of the Ansar (the Helpers), may God's good pleasure be upon them. As for the last stage of their affair, although there is in it some kind of weakness and a measure of softness and gentleness, as there was at the battle of Hunayn and at Ta'if, it is followed by great strength through *itbaq* (emphasis) and elevation and fame that fills the horizons, as the whistling of the **sad** indicates. This is the case for the people of God in general, those mentioned in this surah and others.

As for what pertains specifically to 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, who is the form of this surah and the goal of its allusion [and its biography], the fact that the lingual letters among these letters, most of them, three of them, is an indication that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, through what was given to him in himself and in his offspring, and the tongue of truth mentioned in relation to him, is the tongue of this existence, and that the dynasty of his family, among whom is 'Isa, peace be upon him, is in truth and excellence the middle of this existence. Thus Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, or the founders of his law, are in the position of the **qaf**, which is at the far end of the tongue, and it has a great share of its attributes, for because of him the sons of Israel were slain, and he was born in the year of the slaughter. The cause of his emigration and the beginning of his journey to God, exalted is He, was his killing of the Copt, and he was brought near as one who conversed with God. Among its attributes are *jahr*, *shidda*, *infitah*, *isti'la'* and *qalqala* (echoing), and he was deeply rooted in each of the good qualities of these. And Dawud (David), peace be upon him, the second of the possessors of their books, is in the position of the **hamza**, which is further away from the point of articulation of the **ha'**, one of these letters. He was the first of the Children of Israel to combine kingship and prophethood, and he has a share of its attributes: *jahr*, *shidda* and *infitah*, through the kingship, manifestation, victory over enemies and wonders of destiny that were in him. He has a share of its description as *istifal* at the beginning and end of his affair, through his weeping, humility, submissiveness to his Lord and righteousness. So the **kaf** here indicates that 'Isa, peace be upon him, is the second of the two legislators in existence, and the **ha'** is an expression that he is from the lineage of Dawud, peace be upon him, and each of them has a share of the attributes of the letter that indicates him and points to him. The **sad**, which is from the tip of the tongue and is the final of these letters, is an indication, through its *itbaq*, which indicates [the application of the message to all aspects], and through its *isti'la'*, which indicates [the ultimate of greatness], and through its whistling, which indicates the utmost spread and fame, to Muhammad ﷺ, and to the one who establishes his religion and renews it, 'Isa, peace be upon him. The **kaf** also indicates, through its attributes, that at the beginning of 'Isa's, peace be upon him, affair there will be weakness together with strength, and then the **ha'**, which is from the far end of the throat, indicates that his matter will be hidden after that manifestation and concealed by his being raised to heaven. The *istifal* indicates that it is near the lower part, and this is so in the second, through the indication of the rank of the **kaf** and **ha'** in their points of articulation. The **ya'**, through its *jahr*, indicates his manifestation by his descent, and through being from the middle of the tongue indicates his firm establishment in his affairs. Through its elevation over something in that matter, which is the weakness of the followers and their confinement at that time, and through its openness and softness it indicates his manifestation against the Dajjal (Antichrist) among those people whom affliction has exhausted at his descent, and whom harm has touched before his arrival. The predominance of *istifal* over it hints at the affair of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, because of what God revealed to him: "I have brought out servants of Mine against whom no one has the power to fight; so take My servants into the mount." The **'ayn**, through being from the middle of the throat, indicates their confinement, and through its *jahr* indicates that there is no way for the enemy against them and no access to them by any means. Through what it has of intermediacy and *istifal* it indicates their hardship together with a good outcome. Through its openness it gives glad tidings of the coming of the victory after which there is no victory. The **sad**, through its point of articulation, indicates extra strength, and through *hams* and *rakhawa* indicates that it is a strength without violence. Through *itbaq* and *isti'la'* it indicates the religion's dominance over all people, and through whistling it indicates that after that there is nothing but the blowing of the Trumpet for the total destruction of every existing created thing, then for the scattering of graves and the disclosure of what is in the breasts. All of this is from the arrangement of His, glory be to Him, custom regarding His chosen servants in this wondrous manner, and the arrangement of these letters in this ordering that indicates it revolves around complete power, all-encompassing knowledge and dazzling wisdom. He, glory be to Him, has shown them mercy by turning them away from the path of tyrants, which leads to hardness, and by keeping them away from the ways of the arrogant, which inevitably lead to misery. So He made their victory lie in glimmers of defeat, and their defeat in the sum of victory. He protected them from a constant pomp that draws one to haughtiness, height and arrogance, and from a fixed tenderness that leads to humiliation, lowliness and disgrace. Thus the two names fit the one named, and they became perfectly clear in His affair and flourished. This is the meaning of what al-Kalbi said: "It is a praise with which God praised Himself."

**In the name of God**, who is exalted above every blemish of imperfection, able to do whatever He wills. **The Compassionate (al-Rahman)**, whose bounty has encompassed all His creatures. **The Merciful (al-Rahim)**, who has specially favored His righteous servants with what makes their aim prosper.

When the purpose of the surah before it was to show that the Qur'an is upright, without any crookedness, and that its completeness is what brings the order of the first blessing to perfection, and it showed this by presenting the stories under discussion in the finest arrangement, and by unveiling its hidden matters with the most wondrous unveiling, along with other things it arranged in it of wondrous wisdom and strange meanings (p-163) that expose whoever claims that God, glory be to Him, has a son, and it concluded with similar description of the Book, of monotheism (which negates that He can have a son or any other partner in any respect), and of righteous deeds, this surah begins by unveiling stories stranger than those, in fulfilment of the verse ﴿Or did you think that the Companions of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs a wonder?﴾ [al-Kahf: 9]. It does so with an arrangement different from what came before in the earlier surahs, and with particulars not mentioned except in it, without contradicting what preceded. This confirms that His words do not run out, that His wonders cannot be counted or limited, and that if it had come from other than Him it would have contained contradictions. Moreover, its people were the leaders of the monotheists and the guides of the righteous reformers who did righteous deeds, rejected polytheism and laid down that for the people, so their Lord, glory be to Him, had mercy on them. All of them are people whom the Jews, who instructed the Quraysh to question him about the Companions of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn out of obstinacy, hold in esteem. As for all of them except 'Isa, peace be upon him, the matter is clear. As for 'Isa, peace be upon him, they believe that he has not yet come and that he will come, and that people in his days will be upon one religion, in fulfilment of the promise of the Torah, whose statement will come. This is in a manner that implies, in most of it, His exaltation above having a son and His power to resurrect. It begins with the story of one whose birth broke the customary course, in a clear manner showing that a son is needed only by one who is mortal in body or in meaning, who wishes to have a successor in what has become difficult or impossible for him to do. Presenting his story was more fitting, because the rebuke through it is greater, since they directly took part in killing him and in killing his son Yahya, peace be upon them both. It also indicates that righteous deeds founded upon monotheism guarantee the answering of supplication even when it involves breaking the customary course. It then follows with the matter of the one whom they attributed to Him, falsely ascribed to him, and intended to kill, (p-164) in a manner that expresses his status to the utmost degree of expression, with the correct course clearly shown in it, completing the rebuke of the Jews who instructed the Quraysh to question with obstinacy, by pointing to the killing of Zakariyya and Yahya, peace be upon them both, and their claim to have crucified the Messiah whom the Torah announced, for whom they now wait and claim that they are the people most closely connected to him, and to the slander against his mother, may she be far from it, thereby indicating the power to resurrect. In the Torah, at the end of the first book, it is said that Ya'qub, peace be upon him, was informed of his approaching death and said to his sons: "Gather to me, and I will tell you what will befall you in the latter days. Gather and listen, O sons of Ya'qub! Hearken to Israel your father." Then he said: "O Yahudha, your brothers will acknowledge you; your hand will be raised over the necks of your enemies, and the sons of your father will bow down to you. Yahudha is a lion's whelp. As he rescued my son from being killed, he crouched and lay down like a lion and like a lion's cub; who will rouse him from his prey? The sceptre will not depart from the house of Yahudha, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom the dominion belongs, and to him the peoples shall be gathered. He ties his foal to the vine, and his eyes are redder than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk." This is its text. According to the Jews, this is the Messiah, and they call him, in addition, the awaited one and the Mahdi, and they believe that he will help them and deliver them (p-165) from the humiliation they are in. I said to some of them: "I testify that he is the Messiah, son of Maryam, who came, and the Christians followed him, while you opposed him until God raised him up." [He said:] "What is in the Torah is that dominion belongs to him entirely, and 'Isa was not like that." I said: "Dominion will belong to him entirely when he descends following our religion, since he will accept nothing but Islam. The people of the earth will then unite in following him, and through him whoever among you follows him will be made happy, and humiliation will be removed from him. This does not contradict the words of the Torah, for it did not restrict that to the hour of his coming." He did not accept this. Then one day he came to me with a book of theirs explaining the Book of the Prophets, and in his discussion of the good tidings concerning the Messiah he said: "It is not unlikely that he will appear to Israel, then be hidden, then appear, and dominion will belong to him entirely." I said to him: "Look and reflect! This is exactly what I told you before." He was astonished at that. I said: "Obey me and submit!" He reflected, then said: "Until God, exalted, wills."

Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said in his Burhan: When He, exalted, said ﴿Or did you think that the Companions of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs a wonder?﴾ [al-Kahf: 9], and then presented their account, the account of the two men, Musa and al-Khidr, peace be upon them, and the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, He, glory be to Him, followed that with stories containing wonders [that are greater] and with a more hidden cause. So He opened Surat Maryam with Yahya ibn Zakariyya, and the glad tidings of Zakariyya concerning him after old age, the cutting off of hope, and the barrenness of the wife, until Zakariyya asked, questioning and wondering: ﴿How can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?﴾ [Maryam: 8]. (p-166) He, exalted, answered him that this was easy for Him, and that He would make it a sign for the people, and that this matter is more wondrous than the earlier stories. It is as if it were said: "Or do you think, O Muhammad, that the Companions of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs a wonder? We will inform you of their account and of something more wondrous, stranger, and clearer as a sign, namely the story of Zakariyya concerning his son Yahya, and the story of 'Isa concerning his coming into being without a father, so that it may be known that causes, in reality, do not bring about any of their effects except according to God's custom, and that the act belongs to Him, glory be to Him, not to any cause." To this His saying, exalted, to Zakariyya, peace be upon him, points: ﴿I created you before, when you were nothing﴾ [Maryam: 9]. Then He, glory be to Him, followed the glad tidings of Zakariyya concerning Yahya with the giving to him of judgment while still a child, then with the mention of Maryam and her son, peace be upon them both, and the verses following were connected up to the end of the surah. End of quotation.

Since this surah follows the surah describing the Book, which is the source of the blessing of the first creation, with the utmost uprightness, He opened it with the disjointed letters, just as He opened the surah that follows Umm al-Kitab, the one calling to the straight path, describing the Book as guidance that guarantees uprightness, and the one that follows its description, and (p-167) the one that follows al-An'am, which points to the blessing of the first origination. He said: ﴿Kaf, Ha', Ya', 'Ayn, Sad﴾. They are five letters, corresponding in number to those surahs with it, and they comprise the blessings, describe the Book, and are the possessors of the first blessing and the possessors of the second blessing. Just as al-A'raf, which follows the possessor of the first blessing, opened with four letters corresponding in number to what precedes it, including the Mother (the comprehensive one) and the describer, and the possessor of the first blessing; and just as Al 'Imran, which follows the describer, opened with three letters corresponding in number to the Mother and the describer.

﴿Dhikr﴾ [i.e.] this which I recite to you is a mention of ﴿the mercy of your Lord﴾ [i.e.] the One who bestows kindness upon you with support, by uncovering the hidden matters and revealing what is concealed, ﴿His servant﴾. It is in the accusative (manṣūb) by "raḥmat" (mercy), because it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) constructed with the tā' (the feminine ending), not because the tā' indicates singularity. ﴿Zakariyya﴾ [i.e.] the son of Mathān, as a reward for him for his monotheism and his righteous deed, which hope for meeting his Lord had moved him to perform. The mercy from Him, glorified is He, is assistance, answering of supplication, bringing one to the desired goal, and the like of the fruits of mercy with which His servants are characterized.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 19, verse 3:

﴿إذْ نادى﴾ (p-١٦٨) ظَرْفُ (the adverbial complement, *ẓarf*) الرَّحْمَةِ ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾

Since he (God) first honoured him by mentioning him with mercy and by singling him out through the possessive attribution (*idafa*) of "his Lord" to him, which indicates complete nearness, He said: ﴿a call in secret﴾. That is, just as a loving, close friend does with his beloved who turns toward him, with the intent of addressing him in private confidence, combining the honour of intimate conversation with the sweetness of being alone together in seclusion. So He (glory be to Him) took note of it, for He knows the secret and what is more hidden. It is as if it were said: "What was that call?" So it was said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 4:

﴿He said: "My Lord"﴾, with the particle (of address, yā) omitted, to indicate the utmost closeness. ﴿Indeed my bones have weakened﴾, i.e., have become very feeble. ﴿The bone﴾, i.e., this kind [of substance], which is the strongest part of my body and the foundation of its structure, so how about other than it! [Had he said "bones" in the plural, it would have given the impression that what had weakened was the collection of his bones, not all of them.] ﴿And the head has blazed﴾, i.e., its hair has, from me, ﴿with white hair﴾, while I had never been, in the past, with a young age, ﴿in calling upon You﴾, i.e., in my calling upon You, ﴿my Lord, unblessed﴾. So grant me, this time also, Your favours, as You always did, for the one who does good continues his earlier good with later good. Even though what I am calling for is, customarily, extremely remote, yet You did the like of it with my father Ibrahim, peace be upon him. So this is a supplication, a thanksgiving, and a seeking of tenderness;

Then he (Zakariyya) connected to "﴿Indeed my bones have weakened﴾" [Maryam: 4] his saying: ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali (kinsmen) after me﴾, i.e., the conduct of the relatives, that they would mismanage the succession ﴿after me﴾, i.e., in some part of the time that follows my death. ﴿And my wife has been barren﴾, unable to bear children [at all, as indicated by the verb of being (kānat)]. ﴿So grant me﴾, i.e., so as a consequence of my old age, my weakness, your habituating me to being answered [and], my fear of the bad succession of my relatives, my despair of having a child in the ordinary course because of my wife's sterility, and my reaching such an extreme of old age that I have no movement left in me, I say to You, O You who are capable of everything: grant me ﴿from Yourself﴾, i.e., from the hidden and strange matters that are with You, which You do not bring about along the paths of customary and regular causes, and not from any cause that I know, for the causes of that are absent in my case. ﴿A guardian﴾ [i.e.,] from my own loins, as indicated by "offspring" (dhurriyyah) in the other surah.

And a fuller explanation of this has already been given in Āl ʿImrān.

*Who will inherit from me* in all that I possess of knowledge, prophethood and action; *and will inherit* in addition to that *from the family of Ya'qub* our forefather, of what You have singled them out with of gifts and favoured them with of blessings, of noble characters and lofty dispositions. He specified the name of Ya'qub by following his own example when he said to Yusuf, peace be upon them both: ﴿And He will complete His favour upon you and upon the family of Ya'qub﴾ [Yusuf: 6]. Also, because Isra'il became a designation for all the tribes (asbat), and the calamities had come to predominate over them.

Al-Qadi al-'Adud, in *al-Fawa'id al-Ghiyathiyya*, raised an objection to *yarithu* being a descriptive clause (sifah) on the reading with *raf'* (nominative), because it would entail that his supplication, peace be upon him, was not answered, since Yahya, peace be upon him, was killed during his lifetime, and one is not an heir unless he survives after him. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿So We responded to him and gave him Yahya﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90]. He said: then it is made a resumptive clause (isti'nafiyyah), and nothing follows from that except the failure of his expectation, peace be upon him. This is what was transmitted to me from him, but I hold him above that, because it does not necessitate that his supplication was unfulfilled, nor does one dare to impugn the lofty rank of (a prophet) by falsifying his expectation. For the report of Yahya's being killed before him, if it is from the Prophet (ﷺ) and its chain is sound, then naming the knowledge he took from him during his lifetime an inheritance is a metonymy (majaz mursal) by considering what it ultimately leads to in general, especially since it is possible that Yahya, peace be upon him, taught it to those who lived after his father, peace be upon them both. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) called knowledge an inheritance by way of implicit metaphor (isti'arah tab'iyyah) in his saying, peace be upon him: "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets." There is no doubt that learning knowledge necessarily requires the life of the one from whom it is taken, and there is no prohibition on calling it an inheritance at the time of taking it. This is if it is established that Yahya, peace be upon him, died before Zakariyya, peace be upon him. In that case ﴿from behind me﴾ [Maryam: 5] is interpreted as "in what is absent from him," i.e., I am unable to follow the conduct of my kinsmen (mawali) myself in old age, and I feared their bad conduct when they leave my presence and are out of my sight; so grant me a son who will possess my qualities, and so what he asked for came to pass. But if his death before him is not established by the mentioned way, then it is not established at all, and the objection is entirely removed, for the old histories are only from the Jews, so they are nothing. Moreover, al-Baghawi transmitted at the beginning of the commentary (tafsir) of Surat Bani Isra'il what implies that Zakariyya died before Yahya, peace be upon them both. He said: "The last whom Allah sent among their prophets were Zakariyya, Yahya and 'Isa, peace be upon them, and they were from the house of Dawud, peace be upon him. Zakariyya died, peace be upon him, and it was said: he was killed. When Allah raised 'Isa, peace be upon him, from among them, and they killed Yahya, Allah sent against them a king from the kings of Babel called Khurdush, who marched against them with the people of Babel until he entered the Levant upon them. When he prevailed over them, he ordered a chief of his soldiers called Bayuzardan, the owner of the elephant, and he said: 'I had sworn by my god that if I prevailed over the people of Bayt al-Maqdis, I would surely kill them until their blood flows in the middle of my camp, unless I find no one to kill.' So he ordered him to kill them until that was achieved from them. Bayuzardan entered Bayt al-Maqdis and stood in the place where they used to offer their sacrifices, and he found there blood boiling. He said: 'O Children of Israel! What is the matter with this blood, boiling?' They said: 'This is the blood of a sacrifice of ours which we offered, but it was not accepted from us.' He said: 'You have not told me the truth.' They said: 'If it were as in the first of our times, it would have been accepted from us, but kingship and revelation have ceased from us, and therefore it was not accepted from us.' So Bayuzardan slaughtered seventy-seven hundred of their chiefs over that blood, but it did not calm down. Then he brought seven hundred of their youths and slaughtered them over the blood, but it did not calm down. He ordered seven thousand of their elderly and their wives, and they were slaughtered over the blood, but it did not cool. When Bayuzardan saw that the blood would not calm, he said to them: 'O Children of Israel! Woe to you! Be truthful with me and be patient with the command of your Lord, for you have long ruled the earth doing whatever you wished before I leave not one of you, male or female, who blows the fire, except that I kill him.' When they saw his earnestness and the severity of the killing, they confirmed the report and said: 'This is the blood of a prophet who used to forbid us many things that anger Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Had we obeyed him in them, it would have been better for us. He used to inform us of your affair, but we did not believe him, so we killed him, and this is his blood.' Bayuzardan said to them: 'What was his name?' They said: 'Yahya ibn Zakariyya.' He said: 'Now you have told me the truth. By the likes of this your Lord will take revenge upon you.' When Bayuzardan saw that they had been truthful with him, he prostrated and said to those around him: 'Close the gates of the city and expel whoever is here of Khurdush's army,' and he withdrew with the Children of Israel. Then he said: 'O Yahya ibn Zakariyya! My Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people because of you, and what of them has been killed. So be still by Allah's permission before I leave none of your people.' So the blood calmed by Allah's permission, the Exalted. Bayuzardan lifted the killing from them and said: 'I believe in what the Children of Israel believe in, and I am certain that there is no lord besides Him.' He said to the Children of Israel: 'Khurdush ordered me to kill from among you until your blood flows in the middle of his camp, and I am not able to disobey him.' They said to him: 'Do what you have been commanded.' So he ordered them to dig a trench, and he ordered their livestock—horses, mules, donkeys, camels, cows and sheep—and he slaughtered them until the blood flowed into the camp. He ordered that the slain who had been killed before that be thrown upon what he had slaughtered of their animals. Khurdush did not suppose except that what was in the trench was of the Children of Israel. When the blood reached his camp, he sent to Bayuzardan: 'Lift the killing from them,' and he returned to Babel, having all but destroyed the Children of Israel."

This, as you see, is clear evidence that Yahya survived his father, peace be upon them both. Likewise is what preceded in Al 'Imran from the Gospel concerning the story of his birth.

When he concluded his supplication with the words ﴿and make him, my Lord﴾ [i.e., O You who are good to me] ﴿pleasing﴾, meaning, in Your sight with the gaze of approval from You always, until he meets You in that state, it was said in answer to one who seems to ask: What did his Lord, whom he thought well of, say to him?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 7:

﴿O Zechariah, indeed We﴾ i.e., in accordance with the greatness that is Ours, ﴿give you good news﴾ in answer to your supplication. The recitation of the majority other than Hamzah, with the doubling of the consonant (tashdid), is more fitting than the recitation of Hamzah, because of the emphasis (ta'kid) that has been brought, since the one given the good news of it, because of its strangeness, deserves to be denied. ﴿of a boy whose name is Yahya﴾. Then he described him by what he is known for: among what honored him is that this name was reserved for him, so He said: ﴿We have not made for him﴾ before, and perhaps He used the preposition indicating partitiveness (min al-tab'id), specifying the time of the Children of Israel, his people, [So he said -]: ﴿any namesake before﴾. So it is as if it was said: What did he say in response to this great good news? So it was said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 8:

﴿He said﴾, knowing its truth, seeking to confirm it, and savoring its repetition. Was that from his wife or from another? And if it was from her, would they both remain in their state of old age or otherwise, not hasty nor careless? ﴿My Lord﴾, that is, the One who is always good to me by answering my supplication. ﴿How∗﴾, that is, (p-175) from where, how, and in what condition ﴿will I have a boy﴾, one born to me in the utmost strength, vigor, and perfection of manhood? ﴿While my wife has been barren﴾, [that is -] while the situation is that my wife was ﴿barren﴾, not customarily able to bear children, while she and I were both young, so no child came to us because one of the two causes was defective; how then with her when she has grown old! ﴿And I have indeed reached extreme old age﴾, I being ﴿at an extreme of decrepitude﴾, that is, a matter [of dryness -] exceeding the limit, which is the utmost of old age beyond which there is no further degree. From this has arisen such weakness and dryness and desiccation of the limbs as customarily prevents the birth of a child altogether, since both causes are defective together, let alone that he could be described as a boy.

Al-Baghawi said in [Al 'Imran]: al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was one hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old.

Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': This is in the form of an inquiry: will Allah give him a child in that state, or will He turn him into a young man? For Allah, exalted is He, has two arrangements in every act: one is the known one that people follow, which is directing causes toward their effects; the other relates to pure power, and none knows it except those of insight. - End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 9:

﴿He said: "Thus"﴾, that is, the matter is so. Then he gave the reason for it with his words: ﴿"Your Lord said"﴾ [that is,] the One who has accustomed you to goodness, [and he mentioned the content of the speech, saying]: ﴿"It is"﴾, that is, the creation of Yahya from you two in this state, ﴿"for Me"﴾, that is, especially, ﴿"easy"﴾, with no difference in My sight between it and anything else; ﴿"And I created you"﴾, that is, I decreed you, formed you, and [brought you into being].

Since the aim was to liken his situation to having a child from him in spite of the weakness of the cause, by its being made from a drop of semen whose causal power is weak [because it] sometimes bears fruit and sometimes does not, which is the more common case, he used the preposition to indicate this, saying: ﴿"from before"﴾, [that is, before -] this time, ﴿"and you were not"﴾, that is, while the state was that you had not existed. And since peace be upon him was exceedingly eager for the meaning that would be conveyed to him in this glad tidings, He abridged for him, even by omitting the nun, [and in order to establish that he has in himself nothing but pure non-existence, and to negate that he has in himself any existence even at the lowest degree of being, because his state in this wonder calls for reminding him of that, so He said -]: ﴿"you were nothing"﴾ (p-177), that is, [of any account -], then I brought you forth in the form you are in when I willed, and by this it is established that he was born of this wife of his, the barren one, while both of them were elderly.

Then it was said in answer to one who seemed to ask: "What did he say after knowing this?" ﴿He said, "My Lord"﴾, that is, [O You -] the One who has been good to me by bringing me near! ﴿Appoint for me﴾ upon that ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a token that shows me its occurrence. ﴿He said﴾, that is, Allah said: ﴿Your sign﴾ of the occurrence of that is ﴿that you will not speak to the people﴾, that is, you will not be able to speak to them.

Since the surah began with mercy, and the night was the place of its descent, [the Prophet ﷺ said:] "Our Lord descends every night to the lowest heaven and says..." (the hadith), ﴿He said: "For three nights"﴾ [that is, three days with their nights, as indicated by the expression "days" in Al 'Imran], while you are ﴿sound﴾, without muteness, without illness, and without any impediment to speech in general. Rather, you will commune with your Lord during them through His glorification, His praise, the recitation of His Book, and everything of this kind that you wish. Likewise, those other than people, such as the angels and others among the righteous servants of Allah, are included. The sign indicating this was made to be silence from speaking of anything other than the remembrance of Allah, as a proof of his sincerity and of his devoting himself wholly to Allah, to the exclusion of anything else.

﴿So he came out﴾ immediately after Allah had informed him of this, ﴿to his people﴾ [meaning, rising high above the notables among them] ﴿from the mihrab (prayer niche)﴾ in which he had been, which is the front of the sanctuary (haykal) and its noblest part. His tongue was freed for the remembrance of Allah, and it was restrained (p-178) from speaking with people. ﴿And he signalled to them﴾, meaning he gestured with his lips without uttering speech. The Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Rummani said in [Al 'Imran]: "Ramz (gesturing) is signalling with the lips, though it may also be used for signalling with the eyebrows, the eyes and the hands, and the first is the more common. He said: its root meaning is movement." Before him, the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir al-Tabari had said: "As for ramz, its most common meaning among the Arabs is signalling with the lips, though it is sometimes used for signalling with the eyebrows and eyes, and that is not common among them. It may also be said of a hidden speech like a whisper, with lowered voice [ramz]." Then he reported that what is meant here is the movement of the lips, from Mujahid, and this is the end of the quotation. This is also evident regarding revelation, since it is an absolute term covering signal, allusion and hidden speech. So his revelation could be by any of these, since he could not manage anything else in addressing people. But when he turned to communing with his Lord, glory be to Him, his tongue was freed in the best freedom. ﴿That you glorify﴾, meaning establish the declaring of Allah's transcendence and holiness, ta'ala, through prayer and otherwise, ﴿morning and evening﴾. So his wife conceived, as we have said, and bore a son, and he named him Yahya, as We had given him good news of him. Then he grew until he could distinguish, and We said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 12:

﴿O Yahya, take the Book﴾, that is, the Torah, ﴿with strength﴾.

Since prophethood cannot be undertaken, nor can its burden be borne, except when the intellect is firmly established upon reaching maturity (al-ashudd), and since the subjection of its matter before that age is of a great magnitude, the nun (of greatness) in His words ﴿And We gave him﴾ indicates this, with the greatness that belongs to Us (p-179), ﴿the wisdom﴾, that is, prophethood [and understanding of the Torah], ﴿while still a child﴾, because the spirit predominated over him. This extraordinary matter was not required by wisdom to be given to our Prophet ﷺ, because his people had no prior acquaintance with prophethood, so that if they denied him, there would not be for them from among themselves any contradiction that would bind them. Instead, he was given something greater than that: the innate qualities of truthfulness, which made them call him "the Trustworthy" (al-Amin), so that by this they would be deniers of themselves in their denial of him. And by the increased preservation of his Qur'anic miracle after him, it calls people to his religion [with a call that cannot be turned back].

"And [We gave him] "حنانًا" (compassion), that is, mercy, dignity, gravity, tenderness of heart, provision, and blessing, ﴿from Us﴾, from the nearest of the most distant, from Our majesty, without any intermediary of teaching or experience. ﴿And purity﴾, that is, sincerity of intention that overflows into his actions and words. ﴿And he was﴾, that is, by natural disposition and temperament, ﴿God-fearing﴾, one who greatly fears God, exalted is He."

﴿Dutiful﴾, that is, of broad character and kind to ﴿his parents﴾. ﴿He was not﴾ by natural disposition and temperament ﴿tyrannical﴾ toward them or toward anyone else. He then qualified it with the words ﴿disobedient﴾, indicating that he would act as the tyrants do, with harshness, killing, and force against those who deserve it, as God said to the Seal of the Prophets (ﷺ): ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:73]. He was thus obedient to God, upholding His rights and the rights of His servants as they should be upheld. So, blessed is he for what he was given of these qualities that lead to perfection. The use of the intensive form (ṣīgat al-mubālaghah) conveys that what is negated is a natural inclination toward these vices, while whatever falls short of them God removes by purifying the heart or by other means. (p-180)

﴿And peace be upon him﴾ [i.e.,] what peace it is, from Us, ﴿on the day he was born﴾ from every evil that befalls one at birth and afterward in any matter of religion, ﴿and the day he dies﴾ from the agony of death and what follows it. Perhaps He made "peace" indefinite because he was killed, so his body was not kept safe, unlike what comes later concerning Jesus, peace be upon him. ﴿And the day he is raised alive﴾ from everything feared after that, ﴿alive﴾ with a life that is truly life, in which one benefits, in answer to his father's supplication that he be ﴿pleasing﴾. He singled out these times because whoever is safe in them is safe in other times, since they are the most difficult. Al-Tabarani narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every son of Adam will meet [God -] on the Day of Resurrection with a sin, and He may punish him for it if He wills, or have mercy on him, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon them both, for he was a master, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous." The Prophet (ﷺ) then bent down to a speck of earth, took it, and said: "His male organ is like this speck."

Al-Haythami said: In its chain is Hajjaj ibn Sulayman al-Ru'ayni, whom Ibn Hibban and others declared trustworthy, but Abu Zur'ah and others declared weak; the rest of its narrators are trustworthy. He also narrated it from Abdullah ibn Amr and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, but without mention of the male organ. The wording of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, is: "I was in a circle [in -] the mosque discussing the virtues of the prophets," and he mentioned it until he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is not fitting that anyone be better than Yahya ibn Zakariyya." We said: "O Messenger of God! How so?" He said: "Have you not heard how God described him in the Qur'an? ﴿O Yahya, take hold of the Book﴾ [Maryam: 12] — up to His words: [alive -]," and ﴿confirming a word from God, and a master, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous﴾ [Al 'Imran: 39]. "He did not commit a sin, nor did he intend one." Al-Bazzar also narrated it, and in its chain is Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, whom the majority of scholars (jumhur) declared weak, though he [has been declared trustworthy -]; the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.

By moving through these stages, He, glorified is He, pointed to the refutation of those who ascribe a son to God, since such a stage necessarily implies need for both the son himself and his father, and that prevents both the son and the father from being fit for the rank of divinity, which is exalted above need. What has passed in Al 'Imran that must be reviewed has already been covered.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 16:

Since the gist of the story is that he was a son whom God brought forth from a cause that, in its weakness, was close to non-existence, (on his side, he had reached an age and a state of temperament that does not normally accept the act of intercourse; and on his wife's side, she was beyond childbearing age with her despair, having reached about that same age, and being barren she had never accepted pregnancy at all), (p-182) He followed it with a story that is more wondrous than his, in that it contains only one cause, which is the woman, and the cause of maleness is entirely absent from it. This is an indication that He, may He be exalted, creates what He wills sometimes through a strong cause, sometimes through a weak cause, and sometimes without any cause; and whoever is like this is free of need for a son. Since it was incumbent upon the Jews, who ordered the questioning, out of obstinacy, about the stories of the People of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn, to advise the Arabs by informing them that their religion is false because of their polytheism, and they did not do so, they were deserving of rebuke. The story of Zakariyya was greater in rebuking them, through their direct involvement in killing him and killing his son Yahya, peace be upon them both, so He placed it first in the mention, and as a preparation for the matter of Isa, peace be upon him, as its explanation has passed in [Al 'Imran], as a binding obligation upon them to acknowledge him, and upon the Christians to acknowledge that he is a servant, just as each of them acknowledged the matter of Yahya, peace be upon him, and that is because of what combined them both of breaking the normal course of things. The story of Yahya was more fitting than the story of Ishaq, peace be upon them both, for what has preceded, and for the witnessing of those who differed about Isa, peace be upon him, from the two groups, regarding his matter and the matter of Yahya, peace and blessings be upon them, because of their contemporaneity together along with their closeness of lineage. Since the story of Isa, peace be upon him, is more wondrous, He indicated this by changing the context, so He said, conjoining it to what its implied meaning is: "Tell them this," ﴿And mention﴾ - in the form of a command - ﴿in the Book, Maryam﴾, daughter of 'Imran, the maternal aunt of Yahya - as in the Sahih from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik [from Malik -] ibn Sa'sa'a al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with them both, in the hadith of the Night Journey: "When I came through, behold Yahya and Isa, and they are two cousins." Then He substituted for ﴿Maryam﴾ a substitution of inclusion, namely His saying: ﴿when﴾, i.e., mention what happened to her ﴿when she withdrew﴾, i.e., she imposed upon herself to seclude and isolate herself ﴿from her family﴾, taking ﴿a place to the east﴾ away from their place. Her withdrawal was in the direction of the rising of the lights, as an indication of what the Divine Spirit would come to her with.

**﴿So she took﴾**, meaning she took it with intention and deliberate effort. Her use of the preposition indicates the nearness of the place, so he said: **﴿from behind them﴾**, meaning in the nearest part of their place, because she was alone for bathing or some other purpose. **﴿A screen﴾** that would conceal her. **﴿Then We sent﴾**, for a matter that shows Our greatness, **﴿to her Our Spirit﴾**, that is Jibril (peace be upon him), **﴿to her﴾** in order to inform her of what God intends for her of honour, through the birth of 'Isa (peace be upon him) without a father, lest the matter become confused for her, [and -] her thoughts become scattered, so that she would kill herself out of grief. **﴿So he appeared to her﴾**, meaning he took a visible form, for he was a spiritual being who took the form of a corporeal one, **﴿as a man in every way﴾**, well-formed in his creation and handsome in appearance, lest her aversion and fright [and alarm -] from him become too intense. Then he presented the story in the manner of *istinaf* (resumption, a rhetorical term for beginning a new clause that answers an implied question), so he said, indicating her resolve, the sincerity of her worship of God, her turning to Him, and her witnessing of Him such that she does not incline toward anything else:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 18:

﴿Qālat﴾ (p. 184) When she had reached the utmost of beauty, good qualities, righteous attributes and perfection, to the point that it was extremely unlikely that anyone would seek refuge from her, she emphasized it and said: ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful (al-Raḥmān)﴾, my Lord, whose mercy is general for all His servants in this world and the next, and who has for us a particular distinction in bestowing mercy and perfecting blessing, ﴿from you﴾. When she perceived in him, by what God had illuminated of her insight and purified of her inner consciousness, piety (taqwā), she roused and stirred him to act upon the meaning of this seeking of refuge by her saying: ﴿If you are God-fearing (taqiyyan)﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19 (chapter 19), verse 19:

﴿He said﴾: Jibril, peace be upon him, answering her with what means: "Indeed I am not one of those whom you fear [that he would be accused -], emphasising this for the sake of her seeking refuge,

﴿I am only the messenger of your Lord﴾, i.e., the One whom you sought refuge in, i.e., so I am [not accused -], possessing what you mentioned and the additional quality of being a messenger. He expressed it with the name "the Lord," which implies kindness, out of gentleness toward her, and because this surah begins with mercy, and among its greatest aims is enumerating the blessings upon His sincere servants. ﴿That I may bestow﴾ by His command, or "that He may bestow," according to the other recitation, ﴿upon you﴾. He placed the complement first to create suspense for the object, so that it would have greater impact on the soul. Then he clarified it, expressing it with what is greater in goodness, more firmly rooted in the category of glad tidings, and more suitable to the aim of the surah, although this does not contradict what was mentioned in [Ali 'Imran] with his words: (p-185) ﴿a boy﴾, i.e., a male child [at the height of -] strength and manhood, ﴿pure﴾, i.e., clean from everything that defiles humans, growing upon goodness and blessing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 20:

﴿She said﴾ [Maryam]: ﴿"How"﴾, that is, from where and how, ﴿"will I have a boy"﴾ whom I bear, ﴿"when no man has touched me"﴾ in lawful marriage at all, nor in any other way, whether by a doubtful union or otherwise.

When this matter overwhelmed her, the situation drove her to the utmost haste in conveying what she wished to express, [so that perhaps -] she might be relieved from what she had imagined. The situation became too constricting for her, so she abbreviated, even by deleting the nun from "kāna" (was), in order to make clear that the negation of this meaning is in its most emphatic form. So she said: ﴿"And I was not"﴾. Since the child was the secret of the one who bears him, and since expressing it by what derives from the root of boyhood (ghulma) indicates the utmost completeness of manhood, which requires the utmost strength in the matter of marriage, she denied that there was anything of that in her. So she said: ﴿"unchaste"﴾, that is, [so that it would be -] my habit to be immoral. She did not use "baghiyyah" because of the prevalence of its application to women; it was like "ḥāʾiḍ" (menstruating) and "ʿāqir" (barren) in not requiring the feminine marker [and because baghiyyah is only said of one who is actually characterized by it].

﴿He said﴾ [i.e.] Jibril, peace be upon him: ﴿Thus﴾ [it is], the word I [told you - ] will come to pass.

When the tongue of the situation was saying, "How can it happen without a cause?", he answered with His saying: ﴿He said.﴾ Since this surah is built on mercy, gentleness and kindness toward the servants of the Most Merciful, He used the name of the Lord (Rabb) with which it begins, unlike the surah of Tawhid [Al 'Imran], which begins with the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam). So He said: ﴿Your Lord says it is﴾, i.e., what was mentioned, which is the bringing about of a child in this manner, ﴿easy for Me﴾, i.e., for Me alone; no one other than Me can do it [ - ]. ﴿It is easy﴾ [i.e.] We singled you out for it, so that it would be an honour for you [ - ].

Since that [ - ] is among the greatest extraordinary events (khawariq), He drew attention to it with the plural "We" in His saying, as a continuation of what I have supplied from what the context conveys: ﴿and that We may make him﴾, by Our greatness, ﴿a sign for mankind﴾, i.e., a token of the perfection of Our power over resurrection, more evident than the sign in the case of Yahya, peace be upon him. With it is completed the fourfold division in the creation of human beings: He brought Yahya into existence from a female without a male; Hawwa' (Eve) from a male without a female; Adam, peace be upon him, from neither a male nor a female; and the rest of his offspring from a male and a female together. ﴿And as a mercy from Us﴾ to whoever believes in him in the early part of his time, and to most of creation through faith and deliverance from trials in the later part of his time; unlike the sign of Salih, peace be upon him, because that was a sign of annihilation for the people of misguidance. ﴿And it was﴾ all of that ﴿a matter decreed﴾, i.e., determined and settled, which is in the utmost ease, with no impediment to it at all. He drew attention (p-187) to the swiftness with which the pregnancy was caused by this word, although the estimate is as indicated elsewhere in other surahs: "So he breathed into her shift, and the breath reached her womb."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 22:

﴿So she conceived him﴾. He follows the conception with his words: ﴿So she withdrew with him﴾, that is, she secluded herself, while he was in her womb, going to ﴿a remote place﴾, that is, far from her people, or from the eastern place. By the particle fa' of sequence (fa' al-ta'qib) in his words, he indicates that the birth came close after the conception.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 19, verse 23:

﴿So the pangs of childbirth drove her﴾, i.e., they brought her and compelled her. ﴿The pangs (al-makhad)﴾ are the movement of the child in her womb in preparation for birth. ﴿To the trunk of the palm tree﴾, which is the part that appeared [from her] above the ground and did not reach the branches. It was defined (ʿarrafa) because there was no other palm in that cold land, so it was like a sign (ʿalam) because of the wonder in it. The palm is among the trees least able to endure cold. Perhaps she was driven to it rather than to other trees, despite their abundance, because the palm suits her situation: it bears fruit only through pollination from male palms. So its bearing fruit merely by her shaking it is the most fitting thing for her bearing a child without a father. How much more so when this occurred out of season, and when the palm was dry! Moreover, there are benefits in it through leaning on it and relying on it, and its fresh dates are a comfort (khurse) for women after childbirth and extremely beneficial, among other things.

(p-188) Since this was a matter extremely difficult for her, it was as if it were said: "Would that I knew what her condition was!" So it is said: ﴿She said﴾, because of the fear of disgrace that arose in her: ﴿"Would that I had died"﴾. Since she was in such a state, she indicated the encompassing of time by death, in the sense of non-existence, and so she said, without any preposition: ﴿"before this"﴾, i.e., this great matter, ﴿"and I had been a thing forgotten (nasyan)"﴾, i.e., a thing of the kind that is meant to be forgotten, ﴿"utterly forgotten (mansiyyan)"﴾, i.e., actually abandoned, not coming to mind. Then she bore him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 24:

﴿So he called to her from beneath her﴾, and he is ʿIsa, peace be upon him. ﴿Do not grieve﴾. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami' (al-Lawāmiʿ): "The more correct view is that the period of her pregnancy with him and his birth was a single hour, because he was created in a unique way, and he did not come from a drop of semen that passes through the stages of creation." End of quotation. Ibn Kathir related this and said: "It is strange, reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father." It is supported by the fact that it has not been transmitted in our Book or from our Prophet (ﷺ) that they denounced her during the time of the pregnancy; had they known of it, they would have denounced it, and [had they denounced it,] it would have been transmitted just as the denunciation of the birth was transmitted.

When they denounced the birth, it was as though she had said: "Why should I not grieve?" [and she anticipated what would give her a reason for it]. He said: ﴿Your Lord has placed﴾ [that is,] the One who is good to you ﴿beneath you﴾ ﴿in this land in which there is no flowing water﴾ ﴿a stream﴾, a rivulet of water, a great sign for you that will comfort your soul.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 19, verse 25:

﴿And shake towards you﴾, meaning: cause the *hazz* (shaking), which is pulling by means of movement.

Since the intended purpose is to overwhelm her so as to divert her thoughts from the distress that had befallen her, He made the verb intransitive. It is as though she said: "What should I shake?" For there was nothing in the trunk from which benefit could be expected by shaking it. So He stated plainly what was to be shaken: ﴿the trunk of the palm tree﴾ [which you are beneath, despite its dryness and the fact that it is not the time of its bearing fruit. So it is as though she said: "And why is that?" Then He said -]: ﴿it will drop upon you﴾ from its top ﴿fresh, ripe dates﴾, another great sign that gladdens the soul, dispels grief, and points to innocence. The expression in the form of *tafa"ul* [in the recitation of the majority and of Hamza -] indicates [that -] the dates fall from it repeatedly, and by rights this should not be the case, since she is not qualified for it. This is therefore clearly a matter beyond the normal course of nature. The recitation of the majority with assimilation [*idgham*] (a phonetic merging of consonants) indicates [along with that -] that, despite its strength, the fall almost conceals that it comes from her, because of the trunk's dryness and lack of sap. The recitation of Hamza with the vowel *fatha* and without doubling [*takhfif*] indicates the ease and abundance of its falling. The recitation of Hafs from 'Asim with *damma* and the vowel *kasra* on the *qaf*, as the form of the active participle (*fa'il*), indicates abundance, and it is clear that the falling is from her own action. (p-١٩٠)

Since it was known that she shook the trunk and the ripe dates fell, he followed it with His words: ﴿So eat﴾, meaning: as a consequence of the favour bestowed upon you with water and ripe dates, it is said to you, as an enabling of each of the two, ﴿eat of the ripe dates﴾ ﴿and drink﴾ from the water of the stream ﴿and be comforted﴾, meaning, ﴿settle your eye﴾ with sleep, for the one who is grieved does not sleep, and the eye does not settle as long as it remains awake. It is related from al-Asma'i (al-Asma'i) that the meaning is: let your tears be cool, because the tears of joy are cool, while the tears of grief are hot. The derivation of "qarri" (be comforted) is from qarur, which is cool water. End quote.

The Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz (al-Qazzaz) said in his Diwan: al-Farra' (al-Farra') related that Quraysh and those around them say "qarirtu bihi 'aynan" (with kasra on the eye), meaning "aqarru," and that Asad, Qays and Tamim say "qarartu bihi 'aynan" (with fatha), meaning "aqirru." He said, meaning al-Farra': whoever says "qarirtu" (with kasra) has "qarran," and "qarri 'aynan" (with fatha on the eye) is the well-known recitation. Whoever says "qarartu" (with fatha) recites "qirri 'aynan" (with kasra on the qaf), which is the shadhdh (irregular, anomalous reading), he said, meaning al-Qazzaz: it is the dialect of everyone I have met from the people of Najd. The verbal noun is qurrah and quror. (p-191) What is useful here will come in al-Qasas, and in any case it is a metaphor for contentment of the soul and its readiness to sleep, through sufficiency in this world by food for the body and nourishment for the spirit, by its being a clear sign, and in the Hereafter by honour. This is in the most beneficial manner. It has been said: nothing is better for women after childbirth than ripe dates, and nothing is better for the sick than honey. Then, after this, He followed it with His words, emphasizing it as a notice that most of her sight in those times was of the angels, peace be upon them: ﴿If you see﴾, meaning, O Maryam, ﴿any human being﴾ whom you do not doubt is human, who denounces you, ﴿then say﴾ to that denouncer, as a reply to him, with emphasis, as an alert to innocence, because the innocent person remains calm due to his tranquility, while the doubtful one multiplies his speech and his oaths: ﴿Indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the One whose mercy encompasses all things, who admitted me into it despite my weakness and singled me out with what you have seen of extraordinary signs, ﴿a fast﴾, meaning silence ﴿that frees from every blemish﴾ and abstention from speech. ﴿So I will not﴾, meaning, as a consequence of the vow, that I ﴿will not speak today to any human being﴾, for my speech admits of rebuttal and dispute. ﴿But﴾ the child who speaks on my behalf will be one whose speech cannot be repelled. As for me, I purify myself from disputing with the foolish, so I will speak to none but the angels, or to the Creator, with glorification, sanctification and all other kinds of remembrance. They said: among the most humiliated of people is a fool who finds no one to abuse him. And from (p-192) the indication of this by silence from human speech, together with what was previously mentioned of the allusion, is that it is a pure deterrent.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 27:

﴿Then she came﴾, i.e., when she heard these words, her heart was strengthened and her grief departed, and she came ﴿with him﴾, i.e., with ʿĪsā, ﴿to her people﴾ [though among them there was the power of scheming against everything they wished, the coming of one innocent and certain that God was with him -] ﴿carrying him﴾ [not caring for anyone nor hiding herself -] as if it were said: What did they say to her? It was said: ﴿They said: O Maryam﴾, what is this? Emphasizing, because her state in coming (with him) required the denial of their speech, ﴿you have certainly come﴾ with what we see ﴿a monstrous thing﴾, a severed, abominable matter.

O sister of Harun (Aaron)! In his asceticism, his piety and his chastity [he was a righteous man who lived in her time, or he was the brother of Musa (Moses), peace be upon him]. Your father was not a man of evil [i.e., Imran] at any time of the ages, and your mother was not unchaste [i.e., possessing lewdness, that is, deliberately] at any moment, so that you might follow their example.

﴿فَأشارَتْ﴾ [She pointed] in compliance with what she had been commanded, ﴿إلَيْهِ﴾ [to him, that is, to Jesus, so that they would speak to him and he would answer them on her behalf -]. ﴿قالُوا كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ﴾ [They said, "How can we speak to"] ﴿مَن كانَ في المَهْدِ﴾ [one who is in the cradle], meaning before your gesture, ﴿صَبِيًّا﴾ ["a child"] who has not reached the age of [this -] speech, [which only mature and intelligent adults utter, indeed only prophets -]. The use of "كانَ" (was) indicates that, at the time of the gesture toward him, they did not need to speak to him. Rather, when he heard the exchange and the gesture was completed, there appeared from him a statement (p-١٩٣) that broke the customary pattern of infants and young children [and it is possible that "تامَّةً" (complete) here indicates his capability while still below the age of speech, and the accusative of ﴿صَبِيًّا﴾ is as a circumstantial state -]. Since this expression indicated that, he resumed with his statement:

[i.e. -] Describing himself with qualities that contradict the attributes of the wicked, and as an emphatic response to their denial of his mission, he said: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah﴾, i.e., of the Supreme King who possesses the attributes of perfection, and I worship none other. This is an indication of the correct belief concerning him, and that neither Satan nor desire enslaves him. ﴿He has given me the Book﴾, i.e., the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and other scriptures, despite my young age. ﴿And made me﴾, i.e., in His knowledge, ﴿a prophet﴾, who gives news of what He wills at the time He wills. It was said regarding this: "So I will inform you of it."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 31:

﴿And He has made me blessed﴾ with all kinds of blessings ﴿wherever﴾ (ayna ma) ﴿I may be﴾ in any place ﴿I am﴾ in it.

Since His knowledge, glory be to Him, had preceded that Jesus would be claimed to be divine, He commanded him to say: ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer﴾ as a purification of the soul ﴿and zakat﴾ as a purification of wealth, by action in my own self and by command to others ﴿for as long as I live﴾, so that this would be a proof against those who exalted him, because there is no doubt that one who prays to a god who is not God is not a god.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 19, verse 32:

﴿And dutiful﴾, i.e. [w -] He made me dutiful, meaning generous in character and pure in conduct. (p-194) Since the context concerns her innocence, and the truth is made clear in describing him, he stated her innocence explicitly, saying: ﴿to my mother﴾, i.e. the one whom God honoured by preserving her chastity and by her bearing me without a male. So I have no father other than her. ﴿And He has not made me arrogant, wretched﴾, by my doing the deeds of the arrogant without right. Rather, I act that way only toward someone who deserves it. In this there is an indication that blameworthy arrogance is the act of illegitimate children, because such a person senses the deficiency within himself and wants to compensate for it through his arrogance.

Then he informed of the lasting honor he has from God, indicating that no [enemy] can harm him, and that he is a servant who is not fit to be a god, and [he referred] to the resurrection. So he said: ﴿And peace be upon me﴾, meaning its kind, ﴿the day I was born﴾, so the Satan did not harm me, and whoever is born is not a god. ﴿And the day I die﴾, likewise I die with a complete body and religion; no one can diminish them from me, whoever he may be. ﴿And the day I am raised alive﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, as was mentioned [in] Yahya, peace be upon him, indicating that in humanity he is like him, there is no difference between them at all except that he was born without a father. If the kind of peace is upon him, then cursing is upon his enemies. So it is good news for whoever believed in him, for he is from him, and a warning for whoever denied him. Our Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, did not have a similar extraordinary sign, lest his condition be confused with that of the soothsayers (kuhhan), because his people had no prior acquaintance with extraordinary events except through them. (p-195) When this became fixed in their minds from childhood, its removal became difficult. There was nothing to negate it during childhood, so in place of that he was given the speaking of infants, such as Mubarak al-Yamama and others, and the speaking of dumb animals, and even inanimate things such as stones, the foreleg of a poisoned sheep, the dry trunk [of a palm], and others.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 34:

Since in that which is related of ʿIsa's (ʿIsa) statements and circumstances, which call for the need to move through the various stages of other human beings, and the honor from Allah, there is the greatest clarification of his remoteness from what the Christians claimed of him regarding divinity, and the Jews regarding him being not of right guidance, he drew attention to that, pointing to it with the demonstrative particle of distance, and so he said, beginning: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the great-ranked child, of lofty station, whose circumstances and statements are far removed from the attribute of God [and the attribute of one who doubts his matter]; then he clarified the demonstrative or gave information, saying: ﴿ʿIsa son of Maryam﴾, i.e., alone, there being no fatherhood at all to anyone else in him, and he is of the children of Adam, so he is thus; then he magnified this clarification with another magnification, saying: ﴿a word of truth﴾, i.e., he, meaning his attribution to Maryam alone, is a word of truth, i.e., that which reality corresponds to; or the word is ʿIsa himself, as he is called "a word" in other places, a case of naming the effect by its cause. On this reading (p-196) it is a predicate following a predicate, or an apposition, or the predicate of an omitted subject. [On the reading of ʿAsim and Ibn ʿAmir with the accusative, it is an exhortation, i.e., hold fast to that, which is his attribution to Maryam, peace be upon them both, alone.] Then he marveled at their misguidance regarding it, saying: ﴿about which they doubt﴾, i.e., they are in doubt [a doubt they labor over and dispute about] while his matter is in the utmost clarity and is not a place for doubt at all.

Then he indicated, by His saying, as a refutation of those who went astray, that it is true that he is the son of Maryam and no other, that: ﴿It is not for Allah﴾ — that is, it is not valid, nor possible, nor conceivable by minds, and it is not sound or feasible — since it is among the impossibilities, because it would entail need — ﴿to take﴾ — and since the context requires a general negation, he emphasized it with "min" (from), saying: ﴿any son﴾.

And since taking a son is among the deficiencies, he alluded to this by the general declaration of His transcendence in His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾ — that is, He is exalted above every deficiency, including need for a son or anything else. Then he gave the reason for that in His saying: ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ — whatever matter it may be — ﴿He only says to it, "Be,"﴾ — that is, He wills it and connects His power to it — ﴿and it is﴾, without any need for anything at all. (p-197) How then could He be attributed with need for impregnation, begetting, and gradual nurturing, as the word "taking" indicates?

Since the state of affairs was speaking on behalf of Jesus, peace be upon him, saying (in effect): "God has decreed for me, so I came to be as He willed. I am the servant of God and His messenger, so believe this and do not believe anything else of the falsehoods," He conjoined to it, in the reading of the two Harams (Ibn Kathir and Nafi') and Abu 'Amr, His statement: ﴿And indeed, God﴾, i.e., the One to whom belongs all command, ﴿is my Lord and your Lord﴾, i.e., He has bestowed kindness upon each of us through creation and provision, with no distinction between us in the basis of that. ﴿So worship Him﴾ alone, since He is singular in bestowing beneficence, as I worship Him.

The reading of the rest (with kasra on the inna) is on the basis that it is the speech of Jesus, peace be upon him, already mentioned, and the interjection of what preceded from the speech of God between them is for emphasis and importance.

Since the sharing of creatures in worshipping the Creator through the work of the heart and the limbs, in knowledge and action, is the most just of things, He indicated this by His statement: ﴿This﴾, i.e., what I have commanded you with, ﴿is a straight path﴾, because we have given the truth to its people through correct belief (p-198) and righteous action, and none of us has shown favour over the other in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 37:

Since the straight path is such that it is a cause of unity for every person of sound disposition, He marvels at them for exploiting anything other than that from it. So He says: ﴿Then the factions differed﴾, i.e., as a consequence of this cause of unity, the many factions (al-aḥzāb) differed. Since the difference did not encompass all the matters in their law, He said: ﴿among them﴾, i.e., among the Children of Israel, who were addressed specifically by this, there was no group from other than them in this straight declaration, which one who has the least residue of sound reason should not hesitate to accept. So among them were those who knew that it was the truth and followed it and did not deviate from its correctness, and among them were those who went far astray from it through doubts, of which nothing is weaker. It is related from Qatadah that four rabbis of the Children of Israel gathered: Ya'qub, Nusṭur, Malka and Isra'il. Ya'qub said: "Jesus is God, who descended to the earth." The other three denied him, and the Ya'qubiyya (Jacobites) followed him. Nusṭur said: "Jesus is the son of God," so two denied him, and the Nusṭuriyya (Nestorians) followed him. Malka said: "Jesus is one of three: God is a god, Mary is a god, and Jesus is a god," so the fourth denied him and a sect followed him. Isra'il said: "Jesus is the servant of God, His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him," and a group of the Children of Israel followed him. Then the four fought one another, the believers were overcome and killed, and the Ya'qubiyya prevailed over all. Abu Hayyan and Ibn Kathir mentioned its meaning, and it was narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar from Qatadah. ﴿So woe﴾, i.e., as a consequence of their differing, We say: woe ﴿to those who disbelieved﴾ among them and among others ﴿from the scene of a great Day﴾, in its gathering of all creatures, and what it contains of terrors and calamities.

When that gathering was great, its crowd dense, its ground level, and its sides far-reaching, its situation required that they would not perceive anything beyond what was immediately around them of its terrors. So he said, answering the one who says: "What could they possibly hear or see in it?", informing that their state in the intensity of hearing and sight is worthy of being wondered at: ﴿Hear them and see them﴾, meaning, how intense their hearing is and how penetrating their sight is! ﴿On the day they come to Us﴾, hearing all its terrors, seeing all its conditions, so that by this they perceive everything that their deeds in the world led to their harm on that day, and everything that would have benefited them had they done it. Then they will regret where regret does not benefit them, and they will wish for the impossible, such as returning to the world or the like, so that they may make amends, but they will not be granted that. Rather, they will be driven in every (p-200) matter that harms them, destroys them, and brings them to ruin. By being driven thus, while knowing its harm, they will be blind, mute, and deaf, because they will not benefit from their faculties of perception as they did in the world. That is how it was originally, but he manifested it differently and said: ﴿But the wrongdoers﴾, as an alert to the attribute that placed them in that station, ﴿today are in clear error﴾ [not] hearing and not seeing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 39:

Since what came before was a warning about that scene, the implied meaning is: warn your people about that scene and about what they will hear and see in it. ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾, the scene itself, in that great setting, the Day when the foot slips and regret does not help, for the evildoer over his evil deeds and for the doer of good over not having increased in good.

[Since the day is an object (maf'ul), not a time adverb (zarf), he substituted it, or gave the reason for the warning, and said -]: ﴿when﴾, meaning "at the time when," or "because." [He expressed the future with the past, to signal that it is a certain matter that cannot be avoided, and said -]: ﴿the matter has been decided﴾, meaning its matter has been concluded and finished with the least of affairs and the easiest of matters, and We have determined that it must take place. ﴿And they﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from ﴿warned them﴾ [al-Qamar: 36], meaning: while they [now] are ﴿in heedlessness﴾ of what We have decreed to happen at that time of His affair, having no awareness of any of it, (p-201) but rather they suppose that time is simply life and death without end. ﴿And they do not believe﴾ that it must take place. In the Sahih there is what indicates that the Day of Regret is when Death is slaughtered. Muslim related from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a white-speckled ram. It will be said: 'O people of Paradise! Do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes! This is Death.' It will be said: 'O people of the Fire! Do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes! This is Death.' It will be ordered and it will be slaughtered. Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise! Eternity, with no death!' and 'O people of the Fire! Eternity, with no death!'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited, and in another narration: that is His saying ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter has been decided﴾, the verse.

As for the heedlessness, it is in this world. Ibn Hibban related in his Sahih from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning ﴿when the matter has been decided while they are in heedlessness﴾ that he said: "In this world." Al-Mundhiri said: It is in Muslim with the same meaning at the end of a hadith.

Since inheritance (irth) is taking possession of a thing after the death of its owner, and since He, glory be to Him, had decreed the death of all creatures and that He alone would remain, He expressed that by inheritance, confirming through it the content of the preceding speech. So He said, emphasizing it as a refutation of their saying that time always remains as it is, life for some people and death for others:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 40:
