He said: 'And will I be resurrected after death?' I said: 'Yes!' He said: 'Leave me until I die and am resurrected, for I will surely be given wealth and children, and then I will pay you.' So this verse was revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who﴾ [Maryam: 77] - up to His saying: ﴿alone﴾."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 81:

When Allah, exalted is He, informed of the Resurrection and mentioned that this disbelieving man would come to Him in a state of humiliation, He followed it with the condition of the polytheists regarding the deities they worship. So He said, expressing wonder at them and linking it by conjunction to His saying "and man says": ﴿And they have taken﴾, that is, the disbelievers, and He used the plural because negating might from one does not necessarily entail negating it from more than one, ﴿besides Allah﴾, while it had become clear to them that He is the Supreme King to whom no equal exists, ﴿gods, that they may be for them﴾, that is, for the disbelievers, ﴿a might﴾, so that they may rescue them from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 82:

When he had made clear that neither wealth nor children would grant him honor, and since the benefit of the idols is, beyond doubt, even less than that, He negated it by His saying: ﴿No!﴾ with the particle of rebuke (ar-radʿ), because seeking honor from the source of humiliation, namely from slaves, is [a mistake], for those who gain honor through them are humbled, since they are created with need. Whoever seeks worldly honor will inevitably seek it from slaves, and so he is certainly compelled (p. 245), because they are built on deficiency, to abandon the truth and follow falsehood. Thus the outcome of his affair will be humiliation, however long the term may be, for God Most High may give the forsaken one respite until he reaches, in his abandonment, the point where he deserves the garment of humiliation. Then [He, glory be to Him,] made this clear by what will come from them on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿They will deny﴾, that is, the gods, by a promise that does not fail, however long the time, ﴿their worship﴾, that is, of the polytheists, so they will say to them: ﴿You did not worship us﴾ [Yunus: 28], ﴿when those who were followed will disown those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166], ﴿and they will be against them﴾, that is, the disbelievers. He used the singular to indicate unity of word, such that, from their great solidarity, they are like one thing, and He said: ﴿opponents﴾, meaning enemies, so they will bring humiliation upon them. Likewise the disbelievers do with their partners, saying: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], so enmity arises between them, as God Most High said: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disown others and some of you will curse others﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 25].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 83:

Since it seemed far-fetched to them that they might turn away from them, let alone disbelieve in them, He indicated its occurrence through what is witnessed from them of deeds contrary to the solidity of forbearance that arises from the gravity of knowledge. So He said: ﴿Have you not seen that We​ sent the devils​﴾ with what We possess of greatness, ﴿who We created from fire﴾, [sending them as dominating] by distancing and burning, ﴿upon the disbelievers﴾, that is, those deeply immersed in disbelief (p-246) ﴿inciting them with fierce incitement﴾, that is, stirring them up with vigorous stirring and provoking them into sins and base acts whose ugliness and enormous infamy they do not doubt, and they are the most censurable of people toward their perpetrators and the most reproachful toward those who commit them, provoking them with great agitation, such that in their turning about they are like water boiling in a cooking pot, and like the scattering sparks, which is the thing most contrary to the nature of clay and most compatible with the nature of fire. So when this claim was established, what follows from it is the prohibition against the frivolity of foolishness and the recklessness of ignorance that they were characterized by [so He said]:

Translation:

﴿So do not be hasty against them﴾ with anything by which you would seek relief from them.

Since the watching over of the man's supporter (nāṣir) over his enemy, in his movements and his stillnesses, is the greatest healer for the friend (al-walī) and a gladdener, and the greatest enraging, disturbing, frightening and unsettling thing for the enemy, he gave the reason for that by his saying, indicating that their time is very short by mention of counting: ﴿Indeed, We are counting for them﴾ by Our granting them respite and Our pouring out blessings upon them ﴿a counting﴾, for their breaths and what exceeds them. We do not neglect them in any way. So when their term (ajal) which We set for them comes, We will wipe out their traces and empty their abodes of them. They cannot escape Us. So be patient, for We did not intend by Our giving them respite except their wretchedness and their ruin, not their pleasure and their elevation. This is from the restriction of the attribute to its qualifier exclusively (qaṣr al-mawṣūf ʿalā ṣifatih, ifrād).

When he had explained the final state of the disbelievers regarding their deities and its proof, he followed it with its time, saying: ﴿On the Day﴾, i.e., they will disbelieve in their worship [of those deities] on the day when ﴿We shall gather the God-conscious﴾, i.e., the ones well-rooted (al-'arīqīn) in this attribute (p-٢٤٧). Since the surah of general blessings [al-Nahl] came first, and it was followed by the surah of blessings specific to the believers and some of the general blessings, such as ﴿And We have honoured the children of Adam﴾ [al-Isra': 70], and then by the two surahs specific to the righteous, [al-Kahf] and this one, he said: ﴿to the Most Merciful﴾, so He will admit them to the Abode of Good Pleasure. Thus he mentioned the Name that indicates the generality of mercy, and repeated it in this surah with a repetition that indicates what I have understood. Perhaps this is supported by the opening of al-Nahl with the blessing of speech bestowed upon this human being, which He described as "the disputant" (khasim), and by the ending of this surah with "a people given to contention" (qawman ludda), in that it returns the closing of this [surah], which, in regard to blessings, was one thing, to its opening, ﴿as a delegation﴾, i.e., those who come swiftly, in honour and exalted rank, as delegations come before kings, so they will be in hospitality and honour.

When He had mentioned what indicates the honour of His friends (awliya'), He followed it with what indicates the humiliation of His enemies, saying: ﴿And We will drive the criminals﴾ — that is, those who are guilty through disbelief and other sins — ﴿like cattle, driving them violently, roughly, and hastily﴾ — ﴿to Hell﴾ by the might of the Avenger, the Compeller — ﴿as thirsty ones﴾ — that is, parched with thirst.

Qur'an 19:87: "They will have no power of intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful."

[Al-Biqa'i:] ﴿They will not possess intercession﴾, meaning: neither of the two groups possesses the ability to intercede, nor to be interceded for, ﴿except one who has taken﴾, meaning: who has burdened himself and striven to take ﴿a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾, by means of the faith and obedience to which He granted him success, and for which He promised him that he would intercede or be interceded for. So the verse is of the type called ihtibak (interlocking omission): He mentioned "the Most Merciful" first as an indication of the One who takes vengeance in the second part, and mentioned "Hell" second as an indication of the omission of "Paradise" in the first part. (p-248)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 88:

When he had refuted intercession in general, and the child was the closest intercessor, and they had claimed for Him a child, he refuted their claim concerning it, so that every intercessor, specific and general, would be negated, and thus every honour they sought through the intercession of their gods and others would be negated. He said, conjoining it to His saying ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah﴾ [Maryam: 81] as a consequence of their claim: ﴿And they say﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿The Most Merciful has taken﴾, that is, the One besides whom there is no bestower of blessings, so every one is in need of Him, and He is free of need of every one, ﴿a son.﴾ The Jews said: 'Uzayr; the Christians: the Messiah; and the polytheists: the angels, despite the existence of proofs that it is impossible for Him, glory be to Him.

Then he resumed turning to address them with the strongest denunciation, as a hint at the extremity of anger, and said: ﴿Verily﴾ — that is, by My might! Verily ﴿you have brought a thing hideous﴾ — that is, a great, heavy, abhorrent thing;

Then he showed its heaviness by His saying: ﴿The heavens are about to burst﴾ from its firmness, despite their distance from those who make this claim, ﴿splitting apart﴾, that is, they begin to be split ﴿from it﴾, that is, from this monstrous thing, ﴿and the earth is cleft﴾ beneath them with a wide, penetrating split, ﴿and the mountains collapse﴾, that is, fall swiftly, ﴿crashing down﴾ despite their hardness, like a roof caving in under what it cannot bear of a heavy body, due to

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 91:

﴿That they attribute﴾, i.e., name [someone] ﴿to the Most Merciful﴾, He from whom every other thing is a blessing, ﴿a son﴾. This is the second object, and the first object has been omitted to indicate generality.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 92:

﴿And it is not befitting﴾ meaning: it is not correct and cannot be conceived ﴿for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾. For He is in no way in need of a son, (p-249) and beyond that, it is impossible, because a son is only ever of the same kind as the father (mujanis lil-walid), and none of the blessings is of the same kind as the absolute Bestower of blessings, the Originator of everything other than Himself. Whoever attributes a son to Him has made Him like one of His creatures and removed Him from deserving this name.

Then he established the proof of His independence from that and of its impossibility for Him, to affirm His oneness and to make clear His all-merciful nature. Thereby he demolished the disbelief in an absolute partner, after having demolished the disbelief in specifically having a son. So He said: ﴿There is not any﴾, that is, "there is not anything [of] the rational beings" — so "من" here is an indefinite noun described by an adjective, since it follows "كل" and it follows "رب" ... ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾, those who claimed that they were a son and others. ﴿Except﴾ [and since among the servants there is one who disobeys his master, He expressed it with coming, so He said -]: ﴿coming to the All-Merciful﴾, the one who encompasses all with kindness, that is, submitting to Him [willingly or unwillingly -] in every state and at every time, ﴿as a servant﴾, subjugated, compelled, fearful and hopeful. How then could the servant be a son or a partner? The verse therefore indicates the incompatibility between servanthood and sonship, and it is thus among the evidences for the freeing of a child or a parent when they are purchased.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 94:

Since it is improbable that the knowledge of all creatures would be attained, he follows it with his saying: ﴿Indeed﴾, that is, by Allah, indeed ﴿He has enumerated them﴾, all of them, encompassing them ﴿and counted them﴾. Since this is hardly believable, he emphasizes it with the verbal noun, saying: ﴿with an exact counting﴾, before their creation, from all aspects of the servant and its necessary attributes, so none of them is brought into existence or born, nor is any one of them made to perish or afflicted (p-250) except at the time He has appointed for him. The enumeration may be before existence, in the world of the unseen, and the counting after existence.

Translation of the passage:

"And every one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection" — that is, every single one of them, after being raised up from death — "alone" (fardan), in a state of humiliation, having lost the wealth and children that We had given him in this world as a source of strength and honour for him, because there is no existent being other than Him who is able to protect itself from annihilation. Thus everything is, without doubt, in His grip. How, then, could it come to mind or occur to imagination that any of that could be a son of His, or that He has a partner with Him?

When this ruling encompassed both the obedient and the disobedient, and that was saddening to the people of obedience because they sensed humiliation in both abodes, the soul was moved to know what obedience had benefited them. He resumed the answer to that, giving them good news with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, confirming their claim of faith and their deeds of righteousness, ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint﴾, realized soon at the Pledge of al-'Aqaba (bay'at al-'Aqabah), ﴿for them the Most Merciful﴾, who singled them out with good pleasure after He had encompassed them with blessing, as a reward for their submission to Him, since that submission was either by their own choice or by their consent. ﴿Affection﴾, meaning great love in the hearts of the servants, indicating the affection they have for Him. Al-Asbahani said: "Without any affection on their part, and without their seeking the causes by which people win the affections of hearts, such as kinship, friendship, favour done, or other such things. Rather, it is an invention that begins with His singling out His friends with a special honour, just as He casts terror and awe into the hearts of their enemies, exalting them and magnifying their station." End of quotation. The meaning, and Allah knows best, is that He, glorified is He, does not place in the heart of any of His righteous servants any rancour against them, because affection (wudd), as Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said, is freedom from the will to harm. What will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, in Surat [al-Rum] will make this clearer. Al-Bukhari and Muslim (al-Shaykhan) and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril and says: 'O Jibril! I love so-and-so, so love him.' So Jibril loves him, then he calls out among the people of the heavens: 'Indeed Allah loves so-and-so [so love him],' and the people of the heavens love him. Then acceptance is placed for him on the earth. And when Allah hates a servant, He calls Jibril and says: '[O Jibril -]! I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' So Jibril hates him, then he calls out among the people of the heavens: 'Indeed Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him,' and the people of the heavens hate him. Then enmity is placed for him on the earth."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 97:

Since the sending down of this heavy word, and then its being made easy to memorize and to act upon, was the cause of what was granted to the people of obedience in this world of love, through their adornment and beautification with good deeds and their purification and guarding themselves from evil deeds, which indicates what they have with their Lord of great honor and nearness, and the intended meaning was that the Almighty (al-Jabbar) would bring upon those who disbelieve hatred and humiliation, He informed each of the two groups of what belongs to it, as good news and warning. He said, explaining the cause of this clarification and making it understood: ﴿So We have only made it easy﴾, that is, this Qur'an, which the humans and the jinn were unable to match, the Book that is upright and the revelation that cannot be altered, ﴿in your tongue﴾ by Our sending it down, this clear Arabic, sweet and firm, ﴿that you may give good news thereby to the righteous﴾, who are those who place between themselves and what angers Allah a shield, so they do not nullify a truth nor make falsehood right, and whenever a slip occurs to them, they hasten to return from it [with repentance], with what they have with Us of honor, which is the fruit of the honor indicated by what they have of it in this world, not to grieve them by revealing in it what might suggest equating them with the people of disobedience in both abodes, ﴿and warn thereby a people most contentious﴾, that is, most vehement in dispute, who seek honor through it, because of what they have with Us of humiliation and disgrace arising from the hatred that is caused by evil deeds, and that We will destroy them if they do not turn back from their obstinacy. The one most contentious (al-aladd) is the one who persists in his error and does not return on account of proof, and who engages in whatever evil he is able to commit in opposing the truth. This is not found except in one who despises the one he disputes with and wishes to make the truth falsehood, out of arrogance toward accepting it. Thus applies to him what Muslim related in the Book of Faith of his Sahih, and Abu Dawud in the Book of Clothing of his Sunan, and al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Righteousness of his Jami', and Ibn Majah in the Introduction of his Sunan, from Ibn Mas'ud (p-253) may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"No one who has in his heart an atom's weight of arrogance will enter Paradise." A man said: "A man likes his clothes to be fine and his sandal-thong to be fine." He said: "Indeed Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people." And in another narration: "and belittling people." Both mean contempt. Whoever has this path becomes accustomed to it and persists in it, and so he is deserving that Allah would bring upon him the worst of falsehood: disbelief at the time of death, so Paradise becomes forbidden to him, for whoever grazes around the protected pasture is likely to fall into it. ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right﴾ [al-A'raf: 146], and so on. How humiliated is one who is arrogant toward the truth! And how honored is one who humbles himself to the truth and is proud against falsehood! By my life, Allah has indeed set His practice, and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah: whoever becomes accustomed to boldness in falsehood becomes humbled in truth. To this His saying, exalted is He, in describing His beloved, refers: ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty toward the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 19, verse 98:

Since the implied construction, indicated by the context after the object of "tundhir" (you warn), is: "Indeed We are capable of destroying them and all that We will concerning them," he joined to it His saying: ﴿How many generations have We destroyed﴾, by what We possess of greatness. Since the intended meaning is generality, he made the adverbial expression (p-254) free of the preposition, and he emphasized the predicate by affirming what comes after it, saying: ﴿before them of any generation﴾, who were stronger than them in might, greater in number, and more solid in their equipment. So nothing remains but hearing their reports and witnessing their traces. Then he said, portraying their state and confirming the content of what has passed of their fate: ﴿Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them even a faint sound?﴾ That is, by sight or touch, or hear from them a whisper (rikz), that is, a hidden sound, let alone one that is audible. Thus the surah ends with what it began with: mercy toward His friends, love toward His chosen ones, and blessing toward those who succeeded their enemies after them; following the mercy to both groups through this Book as glad tidings and warning. So mercy settled upon His friends and passed away from His enemies. And Allah is the Granter of success.
